task: Sections 4-8, 12: compiler kernel minimization and the resolution of the Symmetric-cap-Acyclic incompatibility from UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002.

the_reconfiguration.diagnosis: UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002 required the SEED RELATION R ITSELF to be both bipartite (TH-ARBS-001A) AND acyclic/nilpotent (TH-ARBS-001B), producing Symmetric-cap-Acyclic={empty} for any nonempty R. Re-reading how TH-ARBS-001B was ORIGINALLY tested and certified for tilde_G_k (in ARBS-GRAPH-REALIZATION-001): nilpotency was NOT tested on tilde_G_k's own (symmetric, undirected) adjacency matrix. It was tested on a SEPARATE, DERIVED directed transport matrix N, obtained 'by orienting every edge from its lower to higher canonical vertex index.' TH-ARBS-001A and TH-ARBS-001B were therefore ALWAYS applied to two different objects (R itself for bipartiteness; a derived orientation N of R for nilpotency), and UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002 conflated them onto one object (R alone). This is Outcome J from this run's own Section 2 menu: 'multiple representations of one deeper object are being conflated.'
the_reconfiguration.resolution: Split the two axioms back onto their correct objects: TH-ARBS-001A (bipartite) applies to R. TH-ARBS-001B (nilpotent) applies to N := canonical_orientation(R), the transport operator derived from R by orienting every edge from color-class-0 to color-class-1 under R's own (already-required) bipartition. This orientation is canonical (representation-invariant up to the usual global color-swap ambiguity of a bipartition, exactly mirroring the L_k->R_k convention already used for tilde_G_k) and requires no external choice.
the_reconfiguration.theorem_proven_this_run: For EVERY bipartite relation R (any N), the canonical orientation N is automatically nilpotent with N^2=0: all edges of N go from color-0 to color-1 only, so no length-2 directed walk exists in N by construction, regardless of R's own edge count or structure. Verified computationally with ZERO exceptions across all 1+4+23=28 bipartite Gamma-fixed candidates at N=2,3,4 (every single one gave N^2=0 exactly). TH-ARBS-001B THEREFORE ADDS NO INDEPENDENT CONSTRAINT beyond TH-ARBS-001A once correctly applied to the derived object -- it is automatically satisfied, not a separate filter.
the_reconfiguration.consequence_for_symmetric_machinery: R itself is now free to be symmetric (undirected) -- the false incompatibility is resolved IN PRINCIPLE, since bipartite-and-symmetric is not contradictory (e.g. any complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} is both). Recomputed the corrected F_N^derived_v2 := F_N intersected with bipartite ONLY (dropping the mis-applied acyclic-on-R filter): |F_2^derived_v2|=1, |F_3^derived_v2|=4, |F_4^derived_v2|=23 (all rigid, Aut(R)=1).
the_reconfiguration.honest_residual_finding: Despite the incompatibility being resolved IN PRINCIPLE, EMPIRICALLY zero of the bipartite Gamma-fixed candidates at N=2,3,4 are ALSO symmetric (verified: 0/1, 0/4, 0/23). Symmetric Gamma-fixed relations DO exist at these sizes (2, 4, 16 respectively, per UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002) but none of them happen to also be bipartite in this size range -- plausibly because bipartite graphs on this few vertices are too structurally constrained to avoid the automorphisms that break Gamma-fixedness (twin vertices are common in small bipartite graphs). This is reported as an OPEN N-scaling question, not resolved by this reconfiguration -- see the next-dependency note.

kernel_definition.K_star: R subset X*X, a Gamma-fixed (color-refinement-discrete) relation satisfying TH-ARBS-001A (bipartite). TH-ARBS-001B is automatically satisfied by the derived canonical orientation N of R and is NOT a separate condition on R.
kernel_definition.is_R_still_the_kernel_or_something_deepe: TESTED per Section 5: is R derived from something smaller? Checked candidates: operator algebra (no smaller candidate constructed with lower complexity that reconstructs R without extra information -- Aut(R) and Spec(R) are BOTH derivable FROM R, not vice versa, since neither alone determines R up to isomorphism in general -- e.g. multiple non-isomorphic R's can share the same |Aut(R)|=1). No mathematically necessary deeper primitive was found or constructed this run; R remains the primitive layer, WITH THE EXPLICIT CAVEAT that this is a 'not found,' not a proof of non-existence.
kernel_definition.is_the_kernel_single_valued: NO -- per Section 6, forcing exists-unique(K*) is explicitly prohibited without proof, and none exists: |F_N^derived_v2| = 1, 4, 23 at N=2,3,4, strictly growing. The correct closure object is THE FAMILY F^derived_v2 = {F_N^derived_v2}_N, not a single K*. No colimit, inverse limit, or universal-object construction was proven to collapse this family to one object this run (see uoc_master_closure_matrix.json for the explicit OPEN status).

complexity_comparison_at_N_4.note: Reuses the encoding scheme S1 established in UOC-C0-MINIMAL-SEED-CLOSURE-001 for comparability.
complexity_comparison_at_N_4.K_R_plus_derived_N_bits: 16 (N adds ZERO bits -- it is a deterministic function of R's own bipartition, not independent data, exactly as D_R/T_R/C_R were shown to be pure functions of R in the prior run)
complexity_comparison_at_N_4.conclusion: The reconfiguration does not change the complexity ordering established previously: R (plus everything derived from it, now including N) remains strictly cheaper than (D,T,C) taken as independent primitives.
